target.pattern: \bget(?:s|ting)? (?:people|visitors|them) through the door\b|\bgot (?:people|visitors|them) through the door\b

brief.meaningEn: Attract people to enter or visit a venue, often as a first step towards deeper involvement.
brief.meaningZh: 吸引人實際進入或到訪地方，常是進一步投入之前的第一步。
brief.grammar: get people/visitors through the door; got in past; visitor-attraction sense here.
brief.register: Common informal visitor or customer expression.
brief.boundaryZh: 到訪不等於久留、滿意或再來；也不只看過宣傳。不是本課的強行推人穿門。
brief.misconceptionZh: 首次吸引與保持體驗要分開評估；高到訪不單獨證明長期參與。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述讓人到場的措施及其有限結果。

sources.sentence: Free previews may get people through the door.

listening.en: The free preview got people through the door, but the gallery still needed clear displays to help first-time visitors enjoy the full exhibition.
listening.zh: 免費預覽吸引人到場，但畫廊仍需清楚展示，幫首次訪客享受整個展覽。
listening.promptZh: 預覽做到了甚麼，還未保證甚麼？

options.en: It attracted visits but did not by itself ensure a good full exhibition experience.
options.zh: 它吸引到訪，但本身未保證整個展覽體驗良好。

options.en: It only reached people who stayed home and did not visit.
options.zh: 它只接觸到留家、沒有到訪的人。

options.en: It established that everyone would return regularly.
options.zh: 它已確定每個人都會定期再來。

options.en: It made the full exhibition displays unnecessary.
options.zh: 它令完整展覽的展示不再需要。

listening.explanationZh: 到場是第一步，but 後保留完整體驗仍需的工作。

reply.promptZh: 免費預覽對畫廊的第一步有甚麼幫助？
reply.promptEn: How did the free preview help the gallery take a first step?

options.en: It encouraged first-time visitors to come in.
options.zh: 它鼓勵首次訪客進來。

options.en: It got people through the door.
options.zh: 它吸引人真正到訪。

options.en: People who had not visited came to try the preview.
options.zh: 原未到訪的人前來試看預覽。

options.en: It lowered the barrier to making a first visit.
options.zh: 它減低首次到訪的門檻。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述首次到場，不承諾後續回訪；金句用門的意象。

scene.promptZh: 小劇場提供短開放彩排，很多未來過的居民首次入場，但你還不知道他們會否買正場門票。哪句準確？

options.en: The preview proved that all visitors would purchase a season pass.
options.zh: 預覽證明所有訪客都會買季票。

options.en: The preview got people through the door, while later attendance is still uncertain.
options.zh: 預覽吸引人到場，後來是否再來仍未確定。

options.en: Only viewing the online notice counts as entering the theatre.
options.zh: 只看線上公告就算進入劇院。

scene.explanationZh: 首次到場與後續購票不同，需各有資料。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以單獨顯示 get people through the door？

options.en: Visitors arrive after an invitation to an open day.
options.zh: 訪客受開放日邀請後到場。

options.en: New families enter the centre to try an introductory session.
options.zh: 新家庭進中心試體驗課。

options.en: Many people view a notice, but no visits are recorded.
options.zh: 很多人看公告，但未記錄到訪。

contrast.explanationZh: 曝光不同於實際到場；需看行動。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「有人來一次，就代表長期參與成功」。哪句澄清最好？

options.en: A first visit matters, but repeat participation needs separate evidence.
options.zh: 首次到訪重要，但重複參與需另外證據。

options.en: We can count every first visitor as a regular member immediately.
options.zh: 我們可立即把每位首次訪客算作固定會員。

options.en: The introductory attendance replaces the need to review the main experience.
options.zh: 體驗到場人數取代檢視正式體驗的需要。

dialogue.explanationZh: 吸引第一步不等於留住人，完整體驗與回訪仍需查核。

speaking.en: The open day got people through the door, but we still need to make the experience worthwhile.
speaking.zh: 開放日吸引人到場，但我們仍需讓體驗值得。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清首次吸引及後續體驗。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：圖書館原本在上班時間關門，改設晚間開放後，一些在職家長首次到訪；他們會否持續借書仍未知道。用一至兩句英文說明改變怎樣讓人到場，保留長期參與未知。

examples.en: The later opening hours got people through the door, including parents who worked during the day, though regular borrowing is still uncertain.
examples.zh: 延長開放時間吸引人到場，包括白天工作的家長，但是否定期借書仍未確定。

examples.en: Evening access can get visitors through the door of the library without ensuring that every newcomer becomes a regular borrower.
examples.zh: 晚間開放可吸引訪客到圖書館，但未保證每位新人都成為固定借閱者。

glossary.en: parents who worked during the day

writing.selfCheckZh: 用白天工作與晚間開放的時間門檻，解釋首次到訪；不以首次到場推成長期借書。

takeaways.en: A welcoming introduction can get people through the door.
takeaways.zh: 親切介紹可以吸引人實際到訪。

takeaways.en: The preview got visitors through the door, while thoughtful activities encouraged them to stay.
takeaways.zh: 預覽吸引訪客到場，用心活動則鼓勵留下。

titleZh: 讓內容生動而有感染力

target.pattern: \b(?:bring|brings|bringing|brought) (?:(?:the artwork|the world|learning|the past|the scene|a story|the story|it|them|the painting|the exhibition|local history|history|the account) )?to life\b

brief.meaningEn: Make an artwork, story, imagined setting or subject feel vivid and engaging.
brief.meaningZh: 令藝術作品、故事、想像場景或主題顯得生動而吸引人。
brief.grammar: bring a story/artwork to life; bring to life an old story; pronoun bring it to life. Past brought.
brief.register: Conventional life metaphor for vivid representation.
brief.boundaryZh: 本課指作品或主題變得生動，不是描述場所因人流而熱鬧；生動不代表虛構變成史實，也不保證每人同樣理解。
brief.misconceptionZh: 聲音、細節或示範可令內容易感受，但需要把新增想像與查證事實分清。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述呈現方法如何帶來生動體驗，不把感染力當準確性證據。

listening.en: The guide’s account of the painter’s working day brought the artwork to life, helping visitors imagine how the colours and details were chosen.
listening.zh: 導賞員敘述畫家工作的一天，令作品生動起來，幫訪客想像顏色與細節如何選擇。
listening.promptZh: 導賞敘述有甚麼作用？

options.en: It made the artwork feel more vivid and understandable to visitors.
options.zh: 它令訪客覺得作品較生動、易理解。

options.en: It only supplied catalogue dates without changing the visitors’ experience of the work.
options.zh: 它只提供目錄日期，沒有改變訪客對作品的體驗。

options.en: It proved every imagined detail about the painter’s day was documented.
options.zh: 它證明畫家當天每項想像細節都有記載。

options.en: It removed the need to view the painting itself.
options.zh: 它取代觀看畫作本身的需要。

listening.explanationZh: 幫助想像及感受是呈現效果，不直接證明每項細節有史料。

reply.promptZh: 導賞員講畫家工作的一天，怎樣幫你看作品？
reply.promptEn: How did the guide’s story about the painter’s day help you view the work?

options.en: It helped me imagine the choices behind the colours.
options.zh: 它幫我想像顏色背後的選擇。

options.en: It made the details feel more vivid and meaningful.
options.zh: 它讓細節較生動有意義。

options.en: It brought the artwork to life for me.
options.zh: 它令作品對我生動起來。

options.en: The explanation connected the picture with a human creative process.
options.zh: 解釋把畫面與人的創作過程連起來。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述感染力及理解；金句是呈現比喻。

scene.promptZh: 歷史展用已查證書信、地圖及朗讀，讓訪客較能想像當年生活，但清楚標出想像重構部分。哪句準確？

options.en: The display brings the past to life while distinguishing evidence from reconstruction.
options.zh: 展示讓過往生動起來，同時區分證據及重構。

options.en: Vivid presentation means reconstruction details no longer need labels.
options.zh: 生動呈現表示重構細節不再需標示。

options.en: Visitors’ interest establishes the accuracy of every dramatic detail.
options.zh: 訪客興趣已確定每項戲劇細節準確。

scene.explanationZh: 呈現效果可與來源區分並行，不以感動代替證據。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最超出 bring a story to life 的意思？

options.en: Details help an audience imagine the setting.
options.zh: 細節幫觀眾想像場景。

options.en: A reading makes the characters feel more vivid.
options.zh: 朗讀令人物較生動。

options.en: The engaging result itself confirms every historical claim.
options.zh: 吸引人的效果本身確認每項歷史宣稱。

contrast.explanationZh: 生動與準確需不同證據，不能由效果直接推真假。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「演出 brings history to life，就不用分事實與改編」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: An engaging scene can replace source notes because interest establishes accuracy.
options.zh: 吸引場景可取代來源註記，因為興趣已確定準確。

options.en: We should keep the vivid presentation and clearly identify what is documented or adapted.
options.zh: 我們應保留生動呈現，同時清楚標出甚麼有記載或經改編。

options.en: Any detail that helps the audience imagine the period should be reported as established fact.
options.zh: 任何幫觀眾想像年代的細節，都應報作已證實事實。

dialogue.explanationZh: 感染力可有用，但不能取消事實與改編的區別。

speaking.en: The letters and readings brought the past to life without hiding which details were reconstructed.
speaking.zh: 信件與朗讀讓過往生動起來，同時沒有隱去哪些細節是重構。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把生動呈現與來源透明結合。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你向新社員解釋一個抽象節奏概念，改用敲擊、動作及簡單示範，讓他們較能感受，但仍要練習才懂。用一至兩句英文描述示範帶來的效果。
writing.selfCheckZh: 描述動作令抽象概念可感受，保留仍需練習；不把有趣就當作全已掌握。

examples.en: The movements and simple demonstration brought learning to life, helping new members feel the rhythm before practising it themselves.
examples.zh: 動作與簡單示範讓學習生動起來，幫新社員親身練習前先感受節奏。

examples.en: Using movement can bring learning to life, but the members still need practice to understand the rhythmic pattern.
examples.zh: 用動作可以讓學習生動起來，但社員仍需練習才理解節奏模式。

takeaways.en: The child’s dramatic reading brought the story to life for the group.
takeaways.zh: 孩子生動的朗讀，讓故事對小組活現起來。

takeaways.en: The museum brought to life an old story through letters and carefully labelled reconstruction.
takeaways.zh: 博物館透過信件及清楚標示的重構，令舊故事生動起來。

brief.meaningEn: Be attracted or become engaged in an experience, story or activity.
brief.meaningZh: 受到吸引，逐漸投入經驗、故事或活動。
brief.grammar: be drawn in by + feature; draw people in (separable active form). This lesson mainly uses passive drawn in.
brief.register: Common figurative phrasal verb.
brief.boundaryZh: 吸引投入不一定受騙、被迫或同意全部觀點；也可指當下興趣而非永久喜好。
brief.misconceptionZh: 願意繼續看不表示已完全理解或評估所有內容；需按具體行為說明投入。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述吸引因素及注意投入，不從興趣推論認同。

listening.en: I was drawn in by the quiet opening of the story and kept reading to find out why the neighbours had stopped speaking.
listening.zh: 我被故事安靜的開場吸引，繼續讀，想知道鄰居為何不再交談。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼顯示說話者受到吸引？

options.en: They stopped after the first line without interest.
options.zh: 他讀第一行後就沒興趣停下。

options.en: They kept reading because they wanted to understand the mystery.
options.zh: 他想理解謎團而繼續讀。

options.en: They had already agreed with every character’s decision.
options.zh: 他已同意每位人物的決定。

options.en: They were required to finish despite finding the opening uninteresting.
options.zh: 他覺得開場無趣，卻被要求讀完。

listening.explanationZh: kept reading to find out 提供投入的具體行為，不是已同意全部角色。

reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼在開場後繼續讀？
reply.promptEn: Why did you continue reading after the opening?

options.en: I wanted to know why the neighbours had fallen silent.
options.zh: 我想知道鄰居為何變沉默。

options.en: The opening made me curious about what followed.
options.zh: 開場讓我對後續好奇。

options.en: I was drawn in by the quiet mystery.
options.zh: 我被安靜的謎團吸引了。

options.en: I became interested in the relationship and wanted an explanation.
options.zh: 我對關係感興趣，想要解釋。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代興趣原因；金句不等於受騙或認同。

scene.promptZh: 你原本只想看一下展板，但一組人的生活片段吸引你留下細讀。哪句有根據？

options.en: I was drawn in by the personal details and stayed to read more.
options.zh: 我被個人細節吸引，留下多讀。

options.en: I had finished evaluating every claim before seeing the details.
options.zh: 我看細節前已評估每項宣稱。

options.en: I stayed only because I was ordered to, despite having no interest.
options.zh: 我毫無興趣，只因被命令才留下。

scene.explanationZh: 留下細讀支持投入，未提供已全評估或被迫的證據。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個理解最不宜只憑 drawn in 得出？

options.en: A feature may have made the person want to continue.
options.zh: 某特色可能令那人想繼續。

options.en: Their attention became engaged.
options.zh: 他的注意力投入了。

options.en: Their interest proves full agreement with the message.
options.zh: 興趣證明完全同意信息。

contrast.explanationZh: 投入與認同不同，內容仍可被批判性評估。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「你被故事 drawn in，就不能再批評它」。哪句澄清最好？

options.en: A story can hold my interest while I still question its ideas or evidence.
options.zh: 故事可以吸引我，同時我仍質疑其想法或證據。

options.en: Enjoying the opening removes any reason to assess the later claims.
options.zh: 喜歡開場會消除評估後來宣稱的理由。

options.en: Once interested, I should report every detail as convincing without checking.
options.zh: 一旦有興趣，我就應不查核而把每項細節報作可信。

dialogue.explanationZh: 興趣及批判閱讀可以並存。

speaking.en: I was drawn in by the personal details, but I still wanted to check the claims.
speaking.zh: 我被個人細節吸引，但仍想查核宣稱。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把投入與判斷分清。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你初次去社區戲劇練習，本只想旁觀，卻因合作遊戲及友善氣氛想加入下一輪，仍未決定長期報名。用一至兩句英文描述當下投入。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出合作及氣氛如何吸引參加下一輪，保留長期報名未定，不由當下興趣推成永久承諾。

examples.en: I was drawn in by the cooperative game and friendly atmosphere, so I joined the next round without yet committing to the whole course.
examples.zh: 我被合作遊戲及友善氣氛吸引，所以加入下一輪，仍未承諾整個課程。

examples.en: I was drawn in by the welcoming practice and keen to try a role, though I had not decided about long-term membership.
examples.zh: 親切練習讓我受到吸引，想試一個角色，雖然未決定長期入會。

takeaways.en: I was drawn in by the speaker’s account of repairing a family boat.
takeaways.zh: 我被講者敘述修復家族小船的經歷吸引。

takeaways.en: I was drawn in by the story even while questioning its ending.
takeaways.zh: 即使質疑結局，我仍被故事吸引。

brief.meaningEn: Involving direct practical participation rather than only observing or studying theory.
brief.meaningZh: 直接參與實際工作，而非只觀看或研讀理論。
brief.grammar: hands-on experience/practice/workshop; common compound adjective, not necessarily work using literal hands alone.

brief.outcomeZh: 能區分觀摩與本人實作，結合適當指引。

listening.en: After watching the demonstration, the learners gained hands-on experience by measuring and assembling their own simple models with guidance.
listening.zh: 看示範後，學習者在指導下量度及組裝自己的簡單模型，取得實作經驗。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼讓這部分是 hands-on？

options.en: They completed practical measuring and assembly themselves.
options.zh: 他們親自量度及組裝。

options.en: They only watched the teacher make a model.
options.zh: 他們只看老師做模型。

options.en: They read instructions but did not use them in an activity.
options.zh: 他們讀指引，但未在活動中運用。

options.en: The guidance was removed because practical work cannot include help.
options.zh: 指導被移除，因實作不能有幫助。

listening.explanationZh: 自己量度組裝是實作；with guidance 不取消親身參與。

reply.promptZh: 看示範後，學生還得到甚麼學習機會？
reply.promptEn: What learning opportunity did students get after the demonstration?

options.en: They practised measuring and assembling their own models.
options.zh: 他們練量度及組裝自己的模型。

options.en: They gained hands-on experience.
options.zh: 他們得到親身實作經驗。

options.en: They applied the instructions themselves rather than only watching.
options.zh: 他們自己運用指引，而不只觀看。

options.en: They tried the process with a guide available.
options.zh: 他們在可獲指導下嘗試流程。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代本人實際做；金句不排除必要協助。

scene.promptZh: 你參加修補工作坊，只看台上老師操作，還未輪到自己做。哪句準確？

options.en: I have already gained practical experience of carrying out the repair myself.
options.zh: 我已取得親自完成修補的實作經驗。

options.en: I have observed a useful demonstration but have not yet had hands-on practice.
options.zh: 我看了有用示範，但尚未親身實作。

options.en: Observation has no value because it does not involve my own practical work.
options.zh: 觀摩沒有價值，因為沒有我親自做。

scene.explanationZh: 觀摩可有用，但不能直接說已親自實作。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 hands-on experience？

options.en: Trying the process yourself with appropriate guidance.
options.zh: 在適當指導下親自嘗試流程。

options.en: Carrying out a task and reviewing what happened.
options.zh: 實際做工作並檢視結果。

options.en: Watching a recording without yet attempting any practical task.
options.zh: 只看錄影，尚未嘗試任何實際工作。

contrast.explanationZh: 本人尚未實做，雖可學理論或觀察，不是親身實作。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「hands-on 就不能問導師」。哪句澄清最好？

options.en: Guidance can support practical learning while the learner still carries out the task.
options.zh: 指導可以支持實作，學習者仍親自做工作。

options.en: The mentor should stop explaining once practical work begins, even when learners have new questions.
options.zh: 開始實作後，即使學習者有新問題，導師也應停止解釋。

options.en: Count only the steps completed without advice as practical experience, leaving out the work done after a mentor’s explanation.
options.zh: 只把沒聽建議就完成的步驟算實作經驗，不計聽導師解釋後自己做的工作。

dialogue.explanationZh: 實作關鍵是本人操作；可以先聽解釋或過程提問，不應因此刪去自己完成的工作。

speaking.en: The workshop offers hands-on practice with clear guidance.
speaking.zh: 工作坊提供有清楚指導的親身實作。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述實作與支援並存。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你想學訪問技巧，不只讀範例；社區活動讓你實際問問題、錄下回應，再與導師檢視。用一至兩句英文說明實作學習。
writing.selfCheckZh: 把本人提問及檢視回應與只讀例子分清，保留導師作用，不說一次訪問就已精通。

examples.en: The community project gives me hands-on experience of interviewing because I ask the questions and review the responses with a mentor.
examples.zh: 社區項目給我訪問實作經驗，因為我親自提問，再與導師檢視回應。

examples.en: Reading examples helped, but the hands-on interviews let me practise listening and follow-up questions in a real conversation.
examples.zh: 讀例子有幫助，但親身訪問讓我在真正對話中練聆聽及追問。

takeaways.en: Hands-on practice helped the learners connect instructions with experience.
takeaways.zh: 親身實作幫學習者把指引與經驗連起來。

takeaways.en: The hands-on interview project combined practical questions with guidance from a mentor.
takeaways.zh: 親身訪問項目把實際提問與導師指導結合。

brief.meaningEn: Move into a place or a staged experience, crossing from outside to inside.
brief.meaningZh: 從外走到地方或營造的體驗之內。
brief.grammar: step into + place/exhibit/environment; step, stepped, stepping. Dominant taught sense is literal entry with an experiential extension.
brief.register: Natural movement construction; distinct from taking over a job or stepping into someone’s shoes.
brief.boundaryZh: 走進可帶來近身體驗，但不表示真回到過去、變成故事人物或可任意移動物件。
brief.misconceptionZh: 外面觀看與在內體驗不同；展覽重構仍是重構，不是所有細節已證實。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述跨入空間及體驗，同時保留現實與重構的界線。

listening.en: Visitors step into a reconstructed village kitchen, where recordings and objects help them imagine daily life without claiming that every detail is original.
listening.zh: 訪客走進重構村屋廚房，錄音與物件幫他們想像日常，但未聲稱每個細節都是原物。
listening.promptZh: 訪客得到甚麼體驗？

options.en: They enter a reconstruction designed to help them imagine everyday life.
options.zh: 他們進入旨在幫助想像日常的重構空間。

options.en: They remain outside and see only a catalogue photograph.
options.zh: 他們留在外面，只看目錄照片。

options.en: Entering confirms that every object is the original historical item.
options.zh: 進入確認每件物品都是歷史原物。

options.en: The guide confirmed that every staged detail matched a complete historical record.
options.zh: 導賞員已確認每個營造細節都符合完整史料。

listening.explanationZh: step into 指走入，reconstructed 及 without claiming 限定重構不是所有原物。

reply.promptZh: 這個展覽讓你怎樣體驗村屋廚房？
reply.promptEn: How did the exhibition let you experience the village kitchen?

options.en: I could enter the reconstructed space.
options.zh: 我可進入重構空間。

options.en: I could step into the kitchen and experience it from within.
options.zh: 我可走進廚房，從內部體驗。

options.en: The display let me move inside rather than view it only from outside.
options.zh: 展示讓我走到內部，而非只在外看。

options.en: I stood among the objects while listening to the recordings.
options.zh: 我站在物件之間，同時聽錄音。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代實際進入；金句不等於穿越時間或可觸碰全部。

scene.promptZh: 你沿入口進入模擬船艙，聽故事並看佈置，仍知道這是展覽。哪句準確？

options.en: I stepped into the reconstructed cabin to explore the display.
options.zh: 我走進重構船艙探索展示。

options.en: I stayed in the corridor and never entered the cabin.
options.zh: 我留在走廊，從未進船艙。

options.en: The experience proves the cabin and all its objects survived unchanged from the past.
options.zh: 體驗證明船艙及全部物件從過去原封不動保存。

scene.explanationZh: 走入是位置及體驗，不提供所有物件原真性的證明。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合本課 step into an exhibit？

options.en: Moving from the doorway into the staged space.
options.zh: 從門口走進營造的空間。

options.en: Viewing only an image online without entering the exhibition.
options.zh: 只在線上看影像，未走進展覽。

options.en: Crossing the entrance to experience the display from inside.
options.zh: 越過入口，從內體驗展示。

contrast.explanationZh: 遠端只看影像不同於實際走進空間。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「step into 重構古村，就表示每個道具都是真古物」。哪句澄清最好？

options.en: Entering the reconstruction replaces the need to check the labels.
options.zh: 進入重構空間取代查告示的需要。

options.en: The immersive feeling establishes the age of every object.
options.zh: 沉浸感已確定每件物件年代。

options.en: We entered a staged space; the labels still tell us what is original or recreated.
options.zh: 我們進入營造的空間；告示仍會說明甚麼是原物或重製。

dialogue.explanationZh: 位置及體驗不同於物件來源，仍需看標示。

speaking.en: We stepped into the reconstructed room while keeping its imagined details separate from the original objects.
speaking.zh: 我們走進重構房間，同時分清想像細節與原物。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述進入空間及來源界線。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：設計課搭出未來共享客廳的實體模型，參加者可走入測試座椅與交流空間，並非已落成住宅。用一至兩句英文說明親身進入模型的體驗。
writing.selfCheckZh: 描述進模型內試看空間的新設計目標，保留模型與落成住宅差別，不把體驗當作計劃已實現。

examples.en: Participants can step into the model living room to explore how the shared space might work; it is a design trial, not a completed home.
examples.zh: 參加者可走進模型客廳，探索共享空間可能如何運作；這是設計試驗，不是已落成住宅。

examples.en: We stepped into the full-size model and discussed the seating from inside, while remembering that the final design may change.
examples.zh: 我們走進原大模型，從內部討論座位，同時記得最後設計可能改變。

takeaways.en: She stepped into the practice room to compare the sound from different seats.
takeaways.zh: 她走進練習室，比較不同座位的聲音。

takeaways.en: We stepped into a model of a future room, not a finished building.
takeaways.zh: 我們走進未來房間的模型，而非已完成建築。

brief.meaningEn: Not receiving much notice or attention from the relevant public, organisation or observers.
brief.meaningZh: 沒有受到相關大眾、機構或觀察者太多注意。
brief.grammar: stay/remain/go under the radar; a detection metaphor, opposite attention direction to127 on people’s radar.
brief.register: Common idiom; lack of notice can be intentional or unintentional.
brief.boundaryZh: 不表示不存在、沒有價值或必定秘密行事；要說清誰沒有注意及何時被發現。
brief.misconceptionZh: 低調與完全無人知道不同；沒有報道也不證明活動沒有參與者。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述不顯眼或未被察覺，保留存在及動機的區別。

sources.sentence: The small exhibition stayed under the radar until summer.

listening.en: The local repair group stayed under the radar for months, helping a few neighbours before a newspaper feature brought wider attention.
listening.zh: 本地維修小組幾個月未受廣泛注意，一直幫少量鄰居，直到報章專題帶來更多關注。
listening.promptZh: 報章專題前，小組是甚麼情況？

options.en: It was active but not widely noticed.
options.zh: 它有活動，但未廣泛受注意。

options.en: It had not yet helped anyone or begun any work.
options.zh: 它尚未幫過人或開始工作。

options.en: It was already the main subject of national coverage.
options.zh: 它已是全國報道主要題材。

options.en: It had been proved to be deliberately hiding misconduct.
options.zh: 它已被證實故意隱藏不當行為。

listening.explanationZh: 幫鄰居表示已活動；under radar 不自動說明保密或不當動機。

reply.promptZh: 小組被報章介紹前，有人知道它嗎？
reply.promptEn: Did anyone know about the group before the newspaper feature?

options.en: A few neighbours knew it, but it was not widely recognised.
options.zh: 少量鄰居知道，但未廣泛認識。

options.en: It stayed under the radar beyond its small local circle.
options.zh: 在小本地圈子以外，它未受廣泛注意。

options.en: It was helping people quietly before the wider publicity.
options.zh: 較廣宣傳前，它已低調幫人。

options.en: It had some local users without much public attention.
options.zh: 它有部分本地使用者，卻少有公眾關注。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都保留已有小圈子知道與未廣泛注意；金句不等於無人知。

scene.promptZh: 工具已被少數班級使用，其他老師未聽過，直到校內分享會才廣受注意。哪句準確？

options.en: It did not exist before the sharing session.
options.zh: 分享會前它不存在。

options.en: It had stayed under the radar outside the early users.
options.zh: 在早期使用者以外，它一直未受注意。

options.en: The lack of publicity established that the tool was ineffective.
options.zh: 缺少宣傳已確定工具無效。

scene.explanationZh: 少數使用與較廣未察覺可並存，未表示無效。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個結論最不宜只憑 under the radar 得出？

options.en: A project may have received little wider attention.
options.zh: 項目可能少有較廣注意。

options.en: The relevant observers may not have noticed a development.
options.zh: 相關觀察者可能未留意一項發展。

options.en: The people involved must be intentionally concealing wrongdoing.
options.zh: 參與者必定故意隱藏不當行為。

contrast.explanationZh: 低注意可以無意造成，動機及不當行為需另外證據。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「under the radar 就等於沒做過任何事」。哪句澄清最好？

options.en: The group could be doing useful work without broad publicity.
options.zh: 小組可以沒有廣泛宣傳，仍在做有用工作。

options.en: No newspaper coverage is enough to conclude there were no activities.
options.zh: 沒有報章報道，已足以斷定沒有活動。

options.en: We should date the group’s first work from the first headline rather than its records.
options.zh: 應按首篇標題日期，而非工作紀錄判斷首次工作。

dialogue.explanationZh: 曝光與活動開始不同，需查看實際紀錄。

speaking.en: The useful project stayed under the radar until a local report drew attention to it.
speaking.zh: 有用項目一直未受廣泛注意，直到本地報道帶來關注。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把知名度與實際工作分清。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：校網一個頁面的小字對部分讀者很難看，問題幾周未被管理員留意，直到有人提供具體例子。用一至兩句英文描述問題原未察覺，別推斷有人故意隱瞞。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用未被管理員留意及後來例子描述察覺轉變，不把低注意直接說成不存在或故意。

examples.en: The small-text problem stayed under the radar for weeks until a reader showed the administrator a clear example.
examples.zh: 小字問題幾周未被察覺，直到讀者給管理員看清楚例子。

examples.en: The difficulty had gone under the radar, so the new report helps us notice a problem without assuming anyone hid it deliberately.
examples.zh: 困難原未被察覺，所以新報告幫我們注意問題，而不先假定有人故意隱藏。

takeaways.en: The small project remained under the radar while its volunteers kept working.
takeaways.zh: 小項目未受廣泛注意，義工仍持續工作。

takeaways.en: A recurring problem can stay under the radar until someone records a clear example.
takeaways.zh: 反覆問題可以一直未被察覺，直到有人記錄清楚例子。

brief.meaningEn: Make new opportunities or routes of participation available.
brief.meaningZh: 讓新的機會或參與途徑變得可用。
brief.grammar: a skill/contact/experience opens doors to/for + opportunity/person; past opened.
brief.register: Common opportunity metaphor.
brief.boundaryZh: 不表示每項機會必然成功，也不必是真正房門；有機會後仍需選擇、準備及符合要求。
brief.misconceptionZh: 建立接觸或技能可以擴大選擇，不是保證被錄取、受聘或立即精通。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述具體新機會及仍需完成的後續步驟。

sources.sentence: Learning another language can open doors.

listening.en: Learning the language opened doors to exchanges with partner schools, but students still had to apply and prepare their projects.
listening.zh: 學會語言帶來與友校交流的機會，但學生仍需申請及準備項目。
listening.promptZh: 語言能力帶來甚麼，而非保證甚麼？

options.en: It guaranteed a place without any application.
options.zh: 它保證毋須申請也獲名額。

options.en: It made exchange opportunities accessible while leaving further requirements.
options.zh: 它讓交流機會可接觸，同時仍有後續要求。

options.en: It replaced the need for any project preparation.
options.zh: 它取代任何項目準備的需要。

options.en: It limited exchanges to the schools’ existing local circle.
options.zh: 它把交流限於學校原有本地圈子。

listening.explanationZh: opened doors 指新途徑；but still apply/prepare 保留要求。

reply.promptZh: 學會那種語言怎樣幫學生參加友校交流？
reply.promptEn: How did learning the language help students join partner-school exchanges?

options.en: It made new exchange opportunities available to them.
options.zh: 它讓他們可接觸新的交流機會。

options.en: It opened doors to partner-school projects.
options.zh: 它帶來友校項目的新機會。

options.en: They could communicate with people involved in the exchanges.
options.zh: 他們可與交流參與者溝通。

options.en: It gave them routes to take part that had been harder to access before.
options.zh: 它給他們原本較難接觸的參與途徑。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明可用途徑，不保證申請結果；金句用門比喻。

scene.promptZh: 一場作品分享讓你認識導師及可申請的工作坊，你還需提交作品。哪句準確？

options.en: The meeting opened doors, though I still need to prepare an application.
options.zh: 見面帶來機會，雖然我仍需準備申請。

options.en: Meeting a mentor confirms that my application has already been accepted.
options.zh: 認識導師確認申請已被接受。

options.en: The new contact removes the workshop’s entry requirements.
options.zh: 新聯繫令工作坊加入要求消失。

scene.explanationZh: 知道可申請途徑與已被接受不同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個結論最不宜由 opened doors 得出？

options.en: A person has gained access to new possibilities.
options.zh: 一個人可接觸新可能。

options.en: The result of every possible application is already guaranteed.
options.zh: 每項可能申請的結果已保證。

options.en: A skill or connection may make participation easier to pursue.
options.zh: 技能或聯繫可能讓人較易爭取參與。

contrast.explanationZh: 機會不等於每項成功，後續要求仍可存在。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「這次經驗 opens doors，所以不用再準備」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: The opportunity itself is enough to show we meet every requirement.
options.zh: 機會本身已足以顯示我們符合每項要求。

options.en: We can treat the introduction as acceptance without checking the application process.
options.zh: 我們可不查申請流程，就把介紹當作接受。

options.en: It creates a route, but we still need to meet the requirements and make a good choice.
options.zh: 它建立途徑，但我們仍需符合要求並作好選擇。

dialogue.explanationZh: 新途徑應配合準備及判斷，不自動實現結果。

speaking.en: The experience opened doors, but I still had to prepare for the opportunities.
speaking.zh: 經驗帶來機會，但我仍需為機會作準備。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再區分獲機會與後續努力。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區禮堂原只接受大型機構申請，現也接受小型業餘團體，你的劇組因而有機會辦首次公開讀劇。你要向組員提議查場地日期及提交方案，還沒有獲批。用一至兩句英文說明新途徑與下一步。
writing.selfCheckZh: 說清政策讓小團體可申請場地，提出查日期及交方案；不把新申請途徑當已獲批。

examples.en: The revised hall policy opens doors for small amateur groups like ours to stage a public reading. We should check the available dates before submitting our proposal.
examples.zh: 禮堂新政策為我們這類小型業餘團體帶來公開讀劇的機會。我們應先查可用日期，再交方案。

examples.en: Accepting applications from amateur groups has opened doors, but we still need approval for our first reading. Let’s prepare a clear plan for the hall team.
examples.zh: 接受業餘團體申請帶來機會，但首次讀劇仍需批准。我們為禮堂團隊準備清楚計劃吧。

takeaways.en: A shared project opened doors to further study for the group.
takeaways.zh: 共同項目為小組帶來繼續學習的機會。

takeaways.en: Learning to communicate clearly can open doors without guaranteeing a particular outcome.
takeaways.zh: 學會清楚溝通可以帶來機會，而不保證某項結果。

titleZh: 形成看不見的參與障礙

brief.meaningEn: Create social, informational or practical barriers that make participation difficult without a physical wall.
brief.meaningZh: 造成社交、資訊或實際障礙，沒有實體牆卻讓參與變難。
brief.grammar: put up invisible walls for/between + people; put is also past; putting doubles t.
brief.register: Transparent wall metaphor for nonphysical barriers.
brief.boundaryZh: 需交代具體機制，不是所有規則或不同意都等於排外；必要清楚規則也可幫助參與。
brief.misconceptionZh: 紙面說歡迎不代表資訊、態度或流程實際容易加入；有難度仍需查明來源。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出無形障礙怎樣出現，並提出針對性的入口改善。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Confusing rules can put up invisible walls for new visitors.

listening.en: The club advertised a welcome, but unexplained jargon and hidden application dates put up invisible walls for newcomers.
listening.zh: 社團宣傳歡迎加入，但未解釋術語及隱藏申請日期，為新人形成無形障礙。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼令新人難以參與？

options.en: Newcomers already know the terms, and the only issue is that all places are full.
options.zh: 新人已懂術語，唯一問題是所有名額已滿。

options.en: The welcome guarantees that the application process is understandable.
options.zh: 歡迎宣傳保證申請流程易明。

options.en: Unclear language and inaccessible timing information create barriers.
options.zh: 不清楚語言及難取得日期資訊造成障礙。

options.en: A clear guide has already answered the newcomers’ questions.
options.zh: 清楚指南已解答新人的問題。

listening.explanationZh: 術語與日期是具體資訊障礙，歡迎語句本身不能消除。

reply.promptZh: 社團說歡迎加入，為甚麼新人仍覺得困難？
reply.promptEn: Why do newcomers still struggle when the club says they are welcome?

options.en: The jargon is unexplained and the dates are hard to find.
options.zh: 術語未解釋，日期難找。

options.en: The process requires information that newcomers cannot easily obtain.
options.zh: 流程需要新人不易取得的資訊。

options.en: The jargon and hidden dates put up invisible walls.
options.zh: 術語與隱藏日期形成無形障礙。

options.en: The welcoming message does not match the inaccessible application details.
options.zh: 歡迎信息與難接觸的申請細節不符。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出實際資訊門檻；金句不是實體建築問題。

scene.promptZh: 工作坊只用圈內縮寫解釋報名，又沒有新人可問的聯絡人，雖然名義上開放。哪句貼切？

options.en: The details put up invisible walls despite the public welcome.
options.zh: 細節即使公開歡迎，仍形成無形障礙。

options.en: The open label alone proves that every newcomer can follow the process.
options.zh: 開放標籤本身證明每位新人都能跟流程。

options.en: The published dates are enough to make the process clear, even though the shorthand remains unexplained.
options.zh: 雖然縮寫仍未解釋，但只要公布日期，流程就已清楚。

scene.explanationZh: 公開歡迎及日期資訊都不能代替可理解的用語與求助管道；題目仍有圈內縮寫及無聯絡人的障礙。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不符合 put up invisible walls？

options.en: Using insider terms without explanation in the only entry guide.
options.zh: 唯一加入指南用圈內詞而不解釋。

options.en: Publishing clear dates, plain instructions and a contact for questions.
options.zh: 公布清楚日期、淺白指引及提問聯絡人。

options.en: Expecting newcomers to know unwritten rules before anyone explains them.
options.zh: 未有人解釋便要求新人懂不成文規則。

contrast.explanationZh: 清楚管道減少資訊障礙，而非形成。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「有規則就一定是 invisible walls」。哪句澄清最好？

options.en: Every condition should be removed before we ask what it is for.
options.zh: 問條件用途前，應先移除每項條件。

options.en: A clear and necessary rule can support participation; we should identify what actually blocks access.
options.zh: 清楚必要規則可支持參與；我們應指出甚麼實際阻礙加入。

options.en: Any disagreement with an entry decision proves the process is inaccessible.
options.zh: 對加入決定有任何不同意，都證明流程不能接觸。

dialogue.explanationZh: 需看機制與必要性，不把規則一概當障礙。

speaking.en: Unexplained rules can put up invisible walls even when a group says it welcomes newcomers.
speaking.zh: 群體即使說歡迎新人，未解釋規則仍可形成無形障礙。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把宣稱歡迎與實際門檻分清。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：新組員有不同口音，老組員反覆開玩笑，讓他不敢提出想法，雖然沒有正式禁止發言。你想改變交流態度並給清楚發言機會。用一至兩句英文描述。
writing.selfCheckZh: 說明態度如何阻礙發言並提出實際機會，不只找正式禁令，也不一概批評所有玩笑或規則。

examples.en: The repeated jokes put up invisible walls for the new member, making him reluctant to share ideas even without a formal ban.
examples.zh: 反覆玩笑為新組員形成無形障礙，即使沒有正式禁止，也讓他不願分享想法。

examples.en: We should stop putting up invisible walls through jokes about accents and give each member a clear chance to contribute.
examples.zh: 我們不應透過口音玩笑形成無形障礙，應給每位成員清楚作貢獻機會。

takeaways.en: The confusing form put up invisible walls for first-time applicants.
takeaways.zh: 混亂表格為首次申請者形成無形障礙。

takeaways.en: Unspoken expectations can put up invisible walls between experienced members and newcomers.
takeaways.zh: 不成文期望可以在資深成員與新人之間形成無形障礙。

notes: Root retains697 build invisible walls as a distinct verb-object collocation frame; related nonphysical-barrier metaphor, not a separate claimed idiom sense.

brief.meaningEn: Enter or visit a place at all, often emphasising a first visit or that no visit has happened.
brief.meaningZh: 確實進入或到訪地方，常強調首次或從未去過。
brief.grammar: set foot in + place; never/before/first often occur; past set foot, not setted.
brief.register: Conventional emphatic entry phrase.
brief.boundaryZh: 不必光腳，也不要求整個人已走遍地方；網上工作或看照片不一定代表實際到訪。
brief.misconceptionZh: 未進過某建築不等於與機構毫無關係；線上貢獻及實際到訪是不同事情。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用到訪事實描述首次經驗，保留參與和地點的區別。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Many local children have never set foot in a gallery.

listening.en: I had volunteered online for the charity for two years before I ever set foot in its office.
listening.zh: 我替慈善機構在線上做了兩年義工，才第一次踏進它的辦公室。
listening.promptZh: 到辦公室之前，說話者與機構有甚麼關係？

options.en: They had no involvement of any kind.
options.zh: 他沒有任何參與。

options.en: They had already contributed remotely for two years.
options.zh: 他已遠端貢獻兩年。

options.en: They visited the office every week during those two years.
options.zh: 兩年間他每周到辦公室。

options.en: They had only read the name and had never done volunteer work.
options.zh: 他只讀過名字，從未做義工。

listening.explanationZh: online volunteer two years 支持實際貢獻，set foot in 強調較後首次到場。

reply.promptZh: 你第一次到辦公室之前，已認識這機構嗎？
reply.promptEn: Did you know the charity before your first visit to its office?

options.en: Yes, I had been volunteering remotely for two years.
options.zh: 有，我已遠端做義工兩年。

options.en: Yes, I knew the charity before I ever set foot in its office.
options.zh: 有，我未踏進辦公室前已認識機構。

options.en: Yes, my work with them began online rather than in the building.
options.zh: 有，與他們的工作先從線上開始，而非大樓內。

options.en: Yes, I had contributed for some time without visiting the office.
options.zh: 有，我未到辦公室前已貢獻一段時間。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都保留關係早於實際到訪；金句不否定遠端工作。

scene.promptZh: 同學長期在網上讀地方博物館資料，今天才第一次親身進去。哪句準確？

options.en: Today is the first time she has set foot in the museum, though she has read about it.
options.zh: 雖然讀過資料，今天是她第一次踏進博物館。

options.en: Reading the website means she had already visited the building physically.
options.zh: 看網站表示她已親身到過建築。

options.en: Her first visit proves that she knew nothing about the collection beforehand.
options.zh: 首次到訪證明她之前對館藏一無所知。

scene.explanationZh: 知識與到場不同；首訪不表示此前無知。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不足以支持 have set foot in the studio？

options.en: Entering the studio for a guided visit.
options.zh: 進工作室參加導賞。

options.en: Joining an activity held inside the studio.
options.zh: 加入在工作室內舉行的活動。

options.en: Watching an online tour while never visiting the physical space.
options.zh: 看線上導覽，從未親身到那空間。

contrast.explanationZh: 遠端看不等於實際進入本課所指工作室。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「未 set foot in 辦公室，就不是義工」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: Ask the charity to disregard the remote tasks because they were not done on site.
options.zh: 請機構不計遠端工作，因為不是現場做的。

options.en: A first visit establishes the exact date every kind of involvement began.
options.zh: 首次到訪已確定所有參與開始的日期。

options.en: Remote work can be a real contribution even before someone visits the office.
options.zh: 人在到辦公室之前，遠端工作也可是真正貢獻。

dialogue.explanationZh: 參與及首次到場是不同時間線。

speaking.en: I knew the organisation online before I ever set foot in its building.
speaking.zh: 我未踏進那大樓前，已在線上認識機構。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清已認識與首次親身進入。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你只看過道具儲藏室的平面圖，尚未進去，卻被問到現場是否容易取物。用一至兩句英文說明親身到訪的限制，並提出先實地查看再判斷。

examples.en: I have never set foot in the storeroom, so I can describe the plan but should visit before judging how easy it is to reach the props.
examples.zh: 我從未踏進儲藏室，所以可描述平面圖，但應先到訪才判斷取道具是否方便。

examples.en: Before I set foot in the storeroom, my account of the layout comes from the plan, not from a personal visit.
examples.zh: 踏進儲藏室之前，我對佈局的描述來自平面圖，而非親身到訪。

writing.selfCheckZh: 清楚交代未去過與資料來自平面圖，先實地查看再判斷取物情況；不把未到訪說成一無所知。

takeaways.en: She had never set foot in the archive before the open day.
takeaways.zh: 開放日前，她從未踏進檔案室。

takeaways.en: You can know a place through accounts before you set foot in it yourself.
takeaways.zh: 你可以親身踏進地方前，先透過敘述認識它。

titleZh: 令人覺得難以進入的領域

brief.meaningEn: A field or social environment that feels inaccessible or difficult for outsiders to understand and enter.
brief.meaningZh: 讓圈外人覺得難理解、難進入的領域或社交環境。
brief.grammar: feel/seem like a closed world; a closed world to + person/group.
brief.register: Figurative world metaphor; may describe perceived as well as actual barriers.
brief.boundaryZh: 不必有正式禁令，也不等於所有人故意排斥；要說清是語言、資訊、態度或個人印象造成距離。
brief.misconceptionZh: 感到陌生不必表示永遠無法加入；清楚介紹、實際邀請或可見例子可改變印象。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述陌生領域的進入感受，區分感覺與已證實禁令。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The specialist language made theatre feel like a closed world.

listening.en: The specialist terms made the theatre feel like a closed world to first-time visitors until a plain-language introduction explained how to join the activities.
listening.zh: 專門術語讓首次訪客覺得劇場是難進的領域，直到淺白介紹解釋怎樣加入活動。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼改變了訪客的進入感受？

options.en: A formal membership restriction was removed, rather than a language barrier being explained.
options.zh: 正式會籍限制被移除，而不是語言障礙獲解釋。

options.en: A clear explanation made an unfamiliar field easier to understand and approach.
options.zh: 清楚解釋讓陌生領域較易理解及接觸。

options.en: The introduction admitted that newcomers were deliberately unwelcome.
options.zh: 介紹承認存心不歡迎新人。

options.en: The introduction kept the activities unexplained and added more insider terms.
options.zh: 介紹仍未解釋活動，加入更多圈內詞。

listening.explanationZh: 淺白介紹提供理解及加入途徑，未提供正式禁令或所有人意圖。

reply.promptZh: 訪客最初為甚麼覺得難以接觸劇場？
reply.promptEn: Why did the visitors initially find the theatre difficult to approach?

options.en: The specialist terms were unfamiliar and unexplained.
options.zh: 專門詞陌生而未解釋。

options.en: They could not see how ordinary newcomers could join.
options.zh: 他們看不到普通新人怎樣加入。

options.en: The unexplained terms made it feel like a closed world to them.
options.zh: 未解釋術語令他們覺得那是難進的封閉領域。

options.en: The information assumed knowledge they did not yet have.
options.zh: 資訊假定他們已具備尚未有的知識。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋陌生與進入困難；金句不直接指控動機。

scene.promptZh: 科學社說歡迎新手，但介紹只用未解釋縮寫，學生感到自己不屬於這裏。哪句有根據？

options.en: The society can feel like a closed world when its introduction assumes insider knowledge.
options.zh: 介紹假定圈內知識時，學會可讓人覺得是難進領域。

options.en: The feeling alone proves that a formal ban exists.
options.zh: 感受本身證明有正式禁令。

options.en: No explanation could ever help a newcomer understand the activities.
options.zh: 任何解釋都永遠不能幫新人理解活動。

scene.explanationZh: 陌生語言造成感受，不必先有禁令，也未表示無法改善。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個結論最不宜只憑 a closed world 的感受得出？

options.en: An outsider may struggle to understand entry points.
options.zh: 圈外人可能難理解加入途徑。

options.en: Unexplained customs may make a field feel distant.
options.zh: 未解釋慣例可能令領域感覺疏遠。

options.en: Every person in the field has been proved to intend exclusion.
options.zh: 領域中每個人都已被證實存心排斥。

contrast.explanationZh: 感受及障礙值得處理，但個別動機需另外證據。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「覺得 a closed world，就永遠不可能加入」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: An unfamiliar first impression establishes that no support could help.
options.zh: 陌生的第一印象已確定任何支援都無助。

options.en: Clear information and a real invitation can change that impression, even if we should still examine actual barriers.
options.zh: 清楚資訊及真正邀請可改變印象，雖然仍應檢視實際障礙。

options.en: We should stop asking about entry routes because the field initially feels distant.
options.zh: 最初感到疏遠，就應停止詢問加入途徑。

dialogue.explanationZh: 感受不是永久結果；可以改善資訊及機會，同時不否定實際門檻。

speaking.en: The field felt like a closed world until someone explained a clear way to begin.
speaking.zh: 有人解釋清楚入門方法之前，這領域像難進的封閉世界。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述進入感受如何改變。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你一直以為機械人活動只屬於天才，覺得自己無法加入；一次歡迎初學者的小組示範讓你知道可以從簡單任務開始。用一至兩句英文描述原有印象及新入口，不否認仍需學習。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出原有自我印象及示範提供的新入口，不把陌生感直接寫成正式禁令或人人故意排斥。

examples.en: Robotics had seemed like a closed world to me, but the beginner session showed a clear way to start with a simple task.
examples.zh: 機械人活動原像我難以進入的領域，但初學體驗顯示可以從簡單任務開始。

examples.en: I once saw robotics as a closed world for a gifted few; the welcoming demonstration helped me see a route in, although I still need to learn.
examples.zh: 我曾把機械人活動看成只屬少數天才的封閉領域；親切示範幫我看到入口，雖然仍需學習。

takeaways.en: The craft had seemed like a closed world before the public demonstration.
takeaways.zh: 公開示範前，工藝原像難進的封閉領域。

takeaways.en: A clear guide helped newcomers approach what had felt like a closed world.
takeaways.zh: 清楚指南幫新人接觸原本感到難進的領域。

titleEn: bring something into the public eye

target.pattern: \b(?:bring|brings|bringing|brought) (?:exhibitions|the exhibition|the project|the issue|local work|it) into the public eye\b

brief.meaningEn: Make something visible to, or noticed by, a wider public.
brief.meaningZh: 讓某事被較廣泛的大眾看見或留意。
brief.grammar: bring a project/issue/exhibition into the public eye; past brought; an attention metaphor.
brief.register: Common public-attention expression.
brief.boundaryZh: 公開注意不等於一致認同或解決；也不表示每個人都已看到，要看傳播範圍。
brief.misconceptionZh: 原本有工作但少人知，得到公開注意後才較多人知道；不是從被注意那天才開始存在。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述曝光及公眾注意的改變，保留評價與行動另待查核。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.expression: bring exhibitions into the public eye
sources.sentence: The festival will bring exhibitions into the public eye.

listening.en: A radio interview brought the exhibition into the public eye, but organisers still needed to explain its themes clearly to new visitors.
listening.zh: 電台訪問讓展覽公開受到注意，但主辦者仍需向新訪客清楚解釋主題。
listening.promptZh: 電台訪問主要帶來甚麼？

options.en: Wider awareness, with explanation still needed.
options.zh: 較廣認知，同時仍需解釋。

options.en: A confirmed agreement from every listener about the themes.
options.zh: 每位聽眾對主題的已確認共識。

options.en: The creation of an exhibition that had not existed before the interview.
options.zh: 創造一個訪問前不存在的展覽。

options.en: A reason to cancel any further visitor information.
options.zh: 取消任何後續訪客資訊的理由。

listening.explanationZh: public eye 說明被更多人注意；仍需解釋，不等於共識或內容已全理解。

reply.promptZh: 電台訪問怎樣改變展覽的曝光？
reply.promptEn: How did the radio interview change the exhibition’s visibility?

options.en: It made more people aware of the exhibition.
options.zh: 它讓更多人知道展覽。

options.en: It brought the exhibition into the public eye.
options.zh: 它讓展覽公開受到注意。

options.en: The display reached people beyond its earlier audience.
options.zh: 展示接觸到原本觀眾以外的人。

options.en: It gave the organisers a wider public audience.
options.zh: 它給主辦者較廣大眾受眾。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明公眾注意擴大，不聲稱全部理解或認同。

scene.promptZh: 街坊修復計劃已做數月，現在本地新聞介紹，更多居民開始知道。哪句準確？

options.en: The report brought the project into the public eye, rather than starting the work itself.
options.zh: 報道讓項目公開受注意，而非開始工作本身。

options.en: The first report establishes that no earlier work existed.
options.zh: 首次報道確定之前沒有工作。

options.en: The report proves every resident supports every part of the plan.
options.zh: 報道證明每位居民支持每部分計劃。

scene.explanationZh: 工作早存在，報道改變可見度，未證明全體支持。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 into the public eye 推斷？

options.en: A subject may receive broader public attention.
options.zh: 主題可能受較廣公眾注意。

options.en: Public awareness can increase while disagreement remains.
options.zh: 仍有分歧時，公眾認知也可增加。

options.en: The underlying problem has already been solved by being noticed.
options.zh: 根本問題因被注意就已解決。

contrast.explanationZh: 曝光與解決不同，後續行動需另看。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「問題公開了，就不需要跟進」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: Publicity is enough to report the underlying issue as resolved.
options.zh: 宣傳已足以把根本問題報作已解決。

options.en: Wider attention can help, but we still need to examine and respond to the issue.
options.zh: 較廣注意可有幫助，但仍需檢視並回應問題。

options.en: We should replace the action plan with a record of how many people saw the report.
options.zh: 我們應以看報道人數紀錄取代行動計劃。

dialogue.explanationZh: 注意是條件或機會，不是已完成處理。

speaking.en: The report brought the issue into the public eye, but the response is still being discussed.
speaking.zh: 報道讓問題公開受到注意，但應對方法仍在討論。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清公眾注意及後續處理。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：學生把校園路線中已觀察到的指示不清問題，整理成公開展板，讓更多人知道；改善方法仍需討論。用一至兩句英文描述注意增加與未完的工作。
writing.selfCheckZh: 描述展板帶來注意，同時保留如何改善未定，不把公開視為已解決。

examples.en: The display brought the issue into the public eye, but the school still needs to discuss how to improve the signs.
examples.zh: 展板讓問題公開受注意，但學校仍需討論怎樣改善告示。

examples.en: By showing the confusing directions, students can bring the issue into the public eye without claiming that the solution is already agreed.
examples.zh: 學生透過展示混亂指路，可讓問題公開受注意，而不宣稱解法已議定。

takeaways.en: The festival brought local work into the public eye.
takeaways.zh: 節慶讓本地作品公開受到注意。

takeaways.en: A careful report can bring the issue into the public eye while leaving room for different responses.
takeaways.zh: 仔細報道可讓問題公開受到注意，同時保留不同應對方法的空間。

brief.meaningEn: Receiving a lot of public attention or being widely known.
brief.meaningZh: 受到很多公眾注意，或廣為人知。
brief.grammar: a high-profile event/person/project; a standard compound adjective.
brief.register: Common neutral description of publicity, not automatic praise.
brief.boundaryZh: 不必品質最高、最有專業知識或人人喜歡；也不必一個地方所有人都知道。
brief.misconceptionZh: 知名度可能吸引注意，但活動的適合度、準確性及效果需分開評估。
brief.outcomeZh: 能區分廣受注意與真正適合目標的證據。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A high-profile exhibition can draw large crowds.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A high-profile exhibition can draw large crowds.

listening.en: The high-profile launch attracted reporters, while the smaller weekly sessions were where most of the learning took place.
listening.zh: 廣受矚目的啟動活動吸引記者，但大部分學習在較小型每周聚會發生。
listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣區分兩類活動？

options.en: The launch received publicity, while quieter sessions did much of the teaching.
options.zh: 啟動活動得到宣傳，較低調聚會承擔不少教學。

options.en: Only publicity can show whether learning occurred.
options.zh: 只有宣傳能顯示有沒有學習。

options.en: The smaller sessions had no participants or teaching.
options.zh: 較小聚會沒有參加者或教學。

options.en: Most teaching happened at the launch, while the weekly sessions mainly generated publicity.
options.zh: 大部分教學在啟動活動，每周聚會主要帶來宣傳。

listening.explanationZh: 記者注意及學習實際發生場所是不同比較，不以曝光代替效果。

reply.promptZh: 啟動活動與平常聚會有甚麼不同？
reply.promptEn: How did the launch differ from the regular sessions?

options.en: The launch attracted more public attention.
options.zh: 啟動活動吸引更多公眾注意。

options.en: The launch was high-profile, while the weekly sessions were quieter.
options.zh: 啟動廣受矚目，每周聚會則較低調。

options.en: Reporters focused on the launch rather than the ordinary teaching sessions.
options.zh: 記者聚焦啟動，而非平常教學聚會。

options.en: The opening was more visible, even though learning continued in smaller groups.
options.zh: 開幕較顯眼，雖然學習在小組繼續。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都區分曝光與平常活動，不把知名度當教學成果。

scene.promptZh: 一場活動得到很多傳媒報道，但你還未評估參加者學習效果。哪句最有根據？

options.en: It is high-profile, though its educational impact still needs review.
options.zh: 它廣受矚目，雖然教育效果仍需檢視。

options.en: The publicity alone confirms excellent learning outcomes.
options.zh: 宣傳本身確認學習成果優秀。

options.en: The coverage proves that quieter events could not teach as much.
options.zh: 報道證明較低調活動不可能教得同樣多。

scene.explanationZh: 曝光可有資料支持，效果比較另需證據。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能單靠 high-profile 得知？

options.en: A person or event receives considerable attention.
options.zh: 人物或活動獲相當注意。

options.en: A public audience is likely aware of the event.
options.zh: 公眾受眾很可能知道活動。

options.en: The person is the best-qualified choice for this specific task.
options.zh: 人物是這項特定工作最合資格的選擇。

contrast.explanationZh: 知名度與針對工作資格不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「high-profile 講者就一定最適合初學班」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: Fame settles teaching fit, so the course level need not be checked.
options.zh: 名氣已決定教學適合度，不需查課程程度。

options.en: We should compare the speaker’s experience and approach with what beginners need.
options.zh: 我們應把講者經驗及方法，與初學者需要比較。

options.en: The speaker’s audience size can replace evidence about explaining basic ideas.
options.zh: 講者受眾數目可取代解釋基本概念的證據。

dialogue.explanationZh: 特定教學需要適合度資料，而非只看曝光。

speaking.en: The project is high-profile, but we still need evidence of its effect.
speaking.zh: 項目廣受矚目，但我們仍需成效證據。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把曝光及實際效果分清。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：學生團隊得到一項廣受報道的創作獎，主辦方想把學生姓名及照片放在公開介紹。你要寫給團隊的訊息，提醒這次曝光很大，刊登前先確認各人同意及所需署名，而非自行把所有照片公開。用一至兩句英文表達。
writing.selfCheckZh: 把已給公眾曝光連到刊登前確認同意及署名，不以受歡迎取代各人選擇，也不宣稱已全部同意。

examples.en: This is a high-profile award, so we should confirm each student’s consent before publishing names and photographs. Public attention does not replace that check.
examples.zh: 這是廣受矚目的獎項，所以刊登姓名照片前應確認每位學生同意。公眾注意不能取代這項核對。

examples.en: The high-profile coverage may bring many new readers to our introduction. Let’s check how each team member wants to be credited before it goes online.
examples.zh: 廣受矚目的報道可能為介紹帶來很多新讀者。上網前，我們先核對每位組員想怎樣署名。

takeaways.en: The high-profile event received more coverage than the routine workshops.
takeaways.zh: 廣受矚目活動獲得比平常工作坊更多報道。

takeaways.en: A high-profile expert may still need to adapt an explanation for a new audience.
takeaways.zh: 廣受矚目專家仍可能需為新受眾調整解釋。

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese translations checked against each English sentence; not independent human approval.

brief.meaningEn: Signs of a place’s current cultural energy, creativity and activity.
brief.meaningZh: 地方當下文化能量、創作及活動的可見跡象。
brief.grammar: feel/get a sense of the cultural pulse of a place; pulse is a body-based metaphor.
brief.register: Expressive cultural description, not a formal measured rate.
brief.boundaryZh: 可從多種小活動感受，不必只看最熱鬧一場；一次觀察也未能代表所有群體及全年。
brief.misconceptionZh: 有活力可有安靜創作，不必人人做同一活動；觀察須說明看見甚麼及範圍。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體活動說明所觀察文化跡象，保留樣本及時段限制。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Street performances give visitors a sense of the city's cultural pulse.

listening.en: The evening offered a glimpse of the town’s cultural pulse, with street poetry, a small rehearsal and a discussion in the bookshop.
listening.zh: 那晚的街頭讀詩、小型排練及書店討論，讓人一窺小鎮文化脈動。
listening.promptZh: 說話者提供甚麼支持？

options.en: Several creative activities observed during one evening.
options.zh: 一晚觀察到的幾種創作活動。

options.en: A complete survey of every resident’s cultural habits across the year.
options.zh: 全年每位居民文化習慣的完整調查。

options.en: Only a plan for future activities, with nothing actually observed that night.
options.zh: 只有未來活動計劃，當晚沒有實際觀察到活動。

options.en: Evidence that culture exists only in the largest street performance.
options.zh: 文化只存在於最大街頭表演的證據。

listening.explanationZh: glimpse 與那晚多種例子支持局部文化活動觀察，未給全年全體資料。

reply.promptZh: 那晚你看到甚麼文化活動跡象？
reply.promptEn: What signs of cultural activity did you notice that evening?

options.en: There were poetry readings, rehearsals and a bookshop discussion.
options.zh: 有讀詩、排練及書店討論。

options.en: Those activities gave me a sense of the town’s cultural pulse.
options.zh: 那些活動讓我感受小鎮文化脈動。

options.en: Different small groups were creating and exchanging ideas.
options.zh: 不同小組在創作及交流想法。

options.en: Several ordinary venues were active with art and conversation.
options.zh: 幾個平常場所都有藝術及交談活動。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都回應觀察到的活動跡象；金句不宣稱全面調查。

scene.promptZh: 新居民在不同日子看見小型排練、地方故事聚會及手作分享，想描述文化跡象，同時知道仍有未見群體。哪句準確？

options.en: These encounters offer a sense of the cultural pulse, not a complete picture of everyone.
options.zh: 這些接觸讓人感受文化脈動，而非所有人的完整圖像。

options.en: These encounters establish that every resident shares the same taste.
options.zh: 這些接觸確定每位居民品味相同。

options.en: Only the loudest performance matters, so quieter exchanges should be excluded.
options.zh: 只有最大聲表演重要，所以應排除安靜交流。

scene.explanationZh: 不同活動可支持感受，仍要保留範圍及多樣性。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以單獨支持對當地 cultural pulse 的具體描述？

options.en: Examples of local creative activities and exchanges.
options.zh: 本地創作及交流活動例子。

options.en: An unexplained claim that the place is lively, with no activity or observation supplied.
options.zh: 未解釋的熱鬧宣稱，沒有提供活動或觀察。

options.en: A visit to several ordinary places where people share new work.
options.zh: 到幾處人們分享新作品的平常場所。

contrast.explanationZh: 描述應有實際文化活動，不只抽象說很熱鬧。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友看一場大演出便說已完全了解全城 cultural pulse。哪句回應最好？

options.en: We should use the largest audience as a substitute for learning about other groups.
options.zh: 應用最大受眾代替了解其他群體。

options.en: A single event gives some evidence, but smaller activities and different communities may add other perspectives.
options.zh: 一場活動提供部分證據，但小活動及不同社群可補充其他視角。

options.en: Quiet creative gatherings cannot add anything because the major show is more visible.
options.zh: 大演出較顯眼，所以安靜創作聚會不能補充任何東西。

dialogue.explanationZh: 一瞥不等於全貌，要保留不同群體及活動。

speaking.en: The small gatherings gave us a sense of the neighbourhood’s cultural pulse.
speaking.zh: 小聚會讓我們感受社區文化脈動。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述觀察到的文化活動跡象。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替社區編每月文化行事曆，手織小組及手寫字聚會每周持續練習和交換作品，卻因規模小而漏列。你想請編輯把它們的固定時段及聯絡方式加入，讓居民找到持續參與的途徑。用一至兩句英文說明。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用持續練習、交流作品支持小組的文化作用，提出具體行事曆資料，保留它們只是文化活動的一部分。

examples.en: The weaving circle and lettering group are part of our cultural pulse, even though their meetings are small. Please add their regular times and contacts to the calendar.
examples.zh: 手織小組及手寫字小組雖聚會規模小，也是我們文化脈動的一部分。請把固定時段及聯絡方式加進行事曆。

examples.en: Our calendar should reflect the cultural pulse of people practising and sharing work each week. Including these groups would help residents find a continuing way to take part.
examples.zh: 行事曆應呈現人們每周練習、分享作品的文化脈動。列入這些小組，會幫居民找到持續參與的途徑。

glossary.en: a continuing way to take part

takeaways.en: The visitor sensed the town’s cultural pulse through small everyday encounters.
takeaways.zh: 訪客透過平常小接觸感受到小鎮文化脈動。

takeaways.en: The cultural pulse was visible in quiet workshops as well as in public performances.
takeaways.zh: 安靜工作坊與公開演出中，都看得到文化脈動。

target.pattern: \b(?:take|takes|taking|took|taken) in (?:something new|the new sights|the scene|the unfamiliar details)\b

brief.meaningEn: Notice and absorb unfamiliar sights or experiences attentively.
brief.meaningZh: 留心注意並感受陌生景象或新體驗。
brief.grammar: take in something new/the scene; past took in. This lesson focuses on attentive sensory experience, not every sense of take in.
brief.register: Common phrasal verb; Oxford take something in includes visual noticing separately from understanding heard/read content.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是欺騙、收留或改衣服；留心感受也不表示已記住全部或完整理解每項資訊。
brief.misconceptionZh: 走得快或到過地方不保證留意細節；感受新事物可慢下來，不以景點數量代替投入。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述留心感受的行為，區分接觸、察覺及完全理解。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A museum visit lets us take in something new.

listening.en: We paused at the unfamiliar market to take in the new sights instead of rushing straight to the next stop.
listening.zh: 我們在陌生市場停下來留心感受新景象，而非直趕下一站。
listening.promptZh: 停下來的目的是甚麼？

options.en: To attend to the unfamiliar scene rather than only pass through it.
options.zh: 留意陌生景象，而不只經過。

options.en: To finish visiting more places without noticing details.
options.zh: 不留意細節地去更多地方。

options.en: To prove complete recall of every sign after one glance.
options.zh: 一瞥就證明完整記得每個告示。

options.en: To identify only the way to the next stop rather than attend to the market.
options.zh: 只找前往下一站路線，而非留意市場。

listening.explanationZh: pause 與不急趕支持留心感受，不是景點數量、完整記憶或只找下一站路線。

reply.promptZh: 你們為甚麼在市場停一會，而不是立刻趕路？
reply.promptEn: Why did you pause at the market instead of hurrying on?

options.en: We wanted to notice the unfamiliar details around us.
options.zh: 我們想留意周圍陌生細節。

options.en: We wanted time to take in something new.
options.zh: 我們想有時間感受新事物。

options.en: The pause let us look carefully rather than just pass through.
options.zh: 停頓讓我們仔細看，而不只經過。

options.en: We wanted to experience the place without rushing.
options.zh: 我們想不匆忙地體驗地方。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明停下來的具體目的；金句是感受而非已全懂。

scene.promptZh: 你首次看一組細緻裝置，放慢腳步觀察材料與光線，還未讀完所有解說。哪句準確？

options.en: I am taking in something new without claiming to have understood every explanation.
options.zh: 我在感受新事物，而不聲稱已懂每項解說。

options.en: My first glance establishes complete understanding of every written note.
options.zh: 我第一瞥已確定完整理解每項文字註解。

options.en: Because I entered the room, I must have noticed every detail already.
options.zh: 因我進房，必定已注意每個細節。

scene.explanationZh: 有留心觀察可與未全懂說明並存。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合本課 take in the scene？

options.en: Pausing to look at unfamiliar details.
options.zh: 停下看陌生細節。

options.en: Rushing past without looking at the surroundings.
options.zh: 匆忙經過，不看周圍。

options.en: Giving yourself time to notice how a place feels and looks.
options.zh: 給自己時間留意地方的感受與景象。

contrast.explanationZh: 沒有注意的趕路不同於留心感受。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「到過十個地方，就一定比慢看一處更能 take in 新事物」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: The stop count alone measures how much of the scene we noticed.
options.zh: 停留地點數目本身衡量我們注意多少景象。

options.en: Any visit is enough evidence that we absorbed every detail.
options.zh: 任何到訪已足以證明吸收每項細節。

options.en: Attentive time matters too; passing many places does not show what we actually noticed.
options.zh: 留心的時間也重要；經過很多地方未顯示實際注意甚麼。

dialogue.explanationZh: 數量與實際注意不同，需看停留及觀察行為。

speaking.en: We slowed down to take in the unfamiliar details.
speaking.zh: 我們放慢，留心感受陌生細節。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友帶你第一次聽小型合唱公開排練，你想專心聽聲音如何配合，而不只拍照記錄到過。用一至兩句英文描述留心感受新體驗，別說已懂所有技巧。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用專心聽聲音如何配合支持新體驗，不以照片或到訪紀錄代替投入，也不聲稱所有技巧全懂。

examples.en: I want to take in something new by listening closely to how the voices blend, rather than only taking a photograph.

examples.en: We gave ourselves time to take in something new at the live rehearsal, without pretending we understood every technique.

titleEn: at the top of someone’s list

brief.meaningEn: Among someone’s highest priorities or preferences.
brief.meaningZh: 某人最優先的考慮或偏好之一。
brief.grammar: be at the top of someone’s list; the list can be figurative, not necessarily written.
brief.register: Common priority-ranking expression.
brief.boundaryZh: 優先不表示唯一因素，也不一定已選定最終方案；多項高度重要考慮可並存。
brief.misconceptionZh: 在實際紙張第一行可能只是編排，不必是最重視；本課要看優先程度語境。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明最高重視項目及仍需兼顧的條件。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.expression: at the top of their list
sources.sentence: Affordable rent is at the top of their list.

listening.en: Easy access was at the top of their list when choosing the venue, though cost and available dates still mattered.
listening.zh: 選場地時，容易到達是他們最優先考慮之一，但費用及可用日期仍重要。
listening.promptZh: 小組怎樣看可達性？

options.en: It was a high priority, alongside other relevant considerations.
options.zh: 它是優先考慮，同時另有相關因素。

options.en: It was irrelevant once cost was mentioned.
options.zh: 提到費用後，它就不相關。

options.en: Its priority meant no other factor could matter.
options.zh: 它優先就表示其他因素不能重要。

options.en: The group changed its main priority from access to cost before deciding.
options.zh: 作決定前，小組把主要優先由可達性改為費用。

listening.explanationZh: at top 指重視，though 保留其他因素，不是名字位置或已選定。

reply.promptZh: 小組選場地時，最重視甚麼？
reply.promptEn: What did the group prioritise when choosing the venue?

options.en: They gave easy access a very high priority.
options.zh: 他們高度重視容易到達。

options.en: Easy access was at the top of their list.
options.zh: 容易到達是他們最優先考慮之一。

options.en: They wanted people to reach the event without unnecessary difficulty.
options.zh: 他們想讓人不需額外困難便可到活動。

options.en: Accessibility was one of their main criteria.
options.zh: 可達性是他們主要標準之一。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出重視項目；金句不排除費用及日期。

scene.promptZh: 學生選義工活動，最看重能學新技能，但仍要配合上課時間。哪句準確？

options.en: Learning new skills is at the top of my list, though the timing still has to work.
options.zh: 學新技能是我最優先考慮之一，雖然時間仍需配合。

options.en: Having a priority means the school timetable no longer matters.
options.zh: 有優先項目表示學校時間表不再重要。

options.en: The school timetable is my only priority; learning new skills is unimportant.
options.zh: 學校時間表是我唯一優先；學新技能不重要。

scene.explanationZh: 優先與仍需配合時間可並存，不是只看排版次序。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句最不宜由 at the top of their list 得出？

options.en: They consider it especially important.
options.zh: 他們視它尤其重要。

options.en: They have identified a main preference.
options.zh: 他們已指出主要偏好。

options.en: All other requirements have been removed.
options.zh: 其他所有要求都已移除。

contrast.explanationZh: 主要重視不取消其他條件。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「這項最優先，所以不必再看其他限制」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: We should choose the first option meeting that priority even if it cannot meet the essential conditions.
options.zh: 即使不符必要條件，也應選首個符合優先項目的選項。

options.en: A priority guides the choice, but the other necessary conditions still need checking.
options.zh: 優先事項引導選擇，但其他必要條件仍需查核。

options.en: If timing also matters, the stated priority cannot really be a priority.
options.zh: 如果時間也重要，所說優先項目就不可能真正優先。

dialogue.explanationZh: 需把重視程度與實際選項條件結合，不憑優先一句就完成決定。

speaking.en: Clear information is at the top of our list, but the timing matters too.
speaking.zh: 清楚資訊是我們最優先考慮之一，但時間也重要。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再表達優先與兼顧。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你設計學習小冊，把文字清楚易讀列為最重要目標之一，但頁數與完成日期仍有限制。用一至兩句英文說明優先及仍需配合的事。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出易讀清楚的優先，仍保留頁數時間，不把最優先說成唯一或已完成選擇。

examples.en: Readable text is at the top of our list, but we still need to meet the page limit and deadline.
examples.zh: 文字易讀是我們最優先考慮之一，但仍需符合頁數及期限。

examples.en: Clarity is at the top of my list for the booklet, alongside a realistic length and completion date.
examples.zh: 小冊中，清楚是我最優先考慮之一，同時也需合理篇幅及完成日期。

takeaways.en: A fair entry process is at the top of their list.
takeaways.zh: 公平加入流程是他們最優先考慮之一。

takeaways.en: Rest is at the top of my list this weekend, though I still have a few tasks to finish.
takeaways.zh: 休息是我這周末最優先考慮之一，雖然仍有幾項工作需完成。

titleZh: 吸引比之前更多人到場

target.pattern: \bdraw(?:s|ing)? bigger crowds\b|\bdrew bigger crowds\b|\bdrawn bigger crowds\b

brief.meaningEn: Attract a larger number of people than a stated or understood comparison.
brief.meaningZh: 吸引比已指出或可理解比較對象更多的人。
brief.grammar: draw bigger crowds than + comparison; past drew; drawn after have/has.
brief.register: Natural collocation for attendance, not a separate opaque idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: bigger 需要比較，未必是巨大人潮；更多人不直接證明較好學習、滿意或較高收入。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可比較周末平日或今年去年，但不可把不同統計口徑隨意混作成長。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說清到場人數比較對象，保留效果另待評估。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Weekend events usually draw bigger crowds.

listening.en: The weekend demonstrations drew bigger crowds than the weekday sessions, but both groups completed the same short activity.
listening.zh: 周末示範比平日時段吸引更多人，但兩組都完成相同短活動。
listening.promptZh: 說話者比較甚麼？

options.en: Attendance at weekend and weekday sessions.
options.zh: 周末與平日時段的到場人數。

options.en: The exact learning gain of every person.
options.zh: 每人確切學習增長。

options.en: A claim that weekday sessions had no visitors.
options.zh: 平日時段完全無訪客的宣稱。

options.en: Revenue earned from two different ticket prices.
options.zh: 兩種不同票價賺取的收入。

listening.explanationZh: bigger crowds 比較到場人數，未提供學習或票價收入資料。

reply.promptZh: 周末示範與平日時段有甚麼到場差別？
reply.promptEn: How did attendance differ between the weekend and weekday demonstrations?

options.en: More people came at the weekend.
options.zh: 周末較多人來。

options.en: The weekend sessions drew bigger crowds.
options.zh: 周末時段吸引更多人到場。

options.en: Attendance was higher for the weekend demonstrations.
options.zh: 周末示範到場人數較高。

options.en: The weekday groups were smaller than the weekend groups.
options.zh: 平日組別人數少於周末。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都作同一到場比較，不把更多推成更有效。

scene.promptZh: 同樣統計入口人數，今年開放日到訪較去年多，你還未評估滿意程度。哪句有根據？

options.en: This year’s event drew bigger crowds than last year’s.
options.zh: 今年活動比去年吸引更多人。

options.en: Higher attendance proves that every visitor was more satisfied.
options.zh: 較高到場證明每位訪客都更滿意。

options.en: The crowd figures show that the admission fee increased.
options.zh: 人數顯示入場費上升。

scene.explanationZh: 同口徑到訪比較可支持人數較多，未提供滿意或費用資料。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以單獨支持 draw bigger crowds？

options.en: Comparable entrance counts show more arrivals this year.
options.zh: 可比較入口統計顯示今年更多人到。

options.en: A session has more online views, but physical attendance has not been measured.
options.zh: 時段有更多網上觀看，但未量度實際到場。

options.en: The later show has a larger attending audience than the earlier one.
options.zh: 後場實際觀眾比前場多。

contrast.explanationZh: 網上觀看不是同一到場口徑，需保留比較對象。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「bigger crowds 就表示教得更好」。哪句澄清最好？

options.en: The attendance count can replace checking what participants learned.
options.zh: 到場人數可取代查核參加者學到甚麼。

options.en: A smaller group cannot have an effective learning experience.
options.zh: 較小組別不能有有效學習體驗。

options.en: It describes how many came; learning quality needs different evidence.
options.zh: 它描述來了多少人；學習品質需要不同證據。

dialogue.explanationZh: 數量與效果不同，不以人潮直接評價學習。

speaking.en: The later session drew bigger crowds, though we have not compared learning outcomes.
speaking.zh: 較後時段吸引更多人，但我們未比較學習成果。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把人數比較及效果分開。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：下次社區木偶演出目前預約人數比上一場同期多，主辦者因此預計可能吸引更多人，請你準備較多座椅及接待人手。你要寫安排訊息，保留預約不等於最後到場人數。用一至兩句英文表達。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以同期較多預約支持有保留的預計，連到座椅人手安排，並承認最後到場仍需核對。

examples.en: The next puppet show may draw bigger crowds than the previous one, judging by the higher bookings so far. We should prepare extra seats and check the final attendance afterwards.
examples.zh: 目前預約較多，下場木偶戲可能比上一場吸引更多人。我們應多備座椅，之後再核對實際到場。

examples.en: We expect the show to draw bigger crowds, so let’s arrange more stewards while keeping the forecast separate from the final count.
examples.zh: 我們預計演出會吸引更多人，所以安排更多接待人員，同時把預測與最後點算分開。

takeaways.en: The open-air show drew bigger crowds than the earlier indoor preview.
takeaways.zh: 露天表演比早前室內預覽吸引更多人。

takeaways.en: A popular event may draw bigger crowds without giving each visitor more time to participate.
takeaways.zh: 受歡迎活動可吸引更多人，卻不一定給每位訪客更多參與時間。

brief.meaningEn: Seem to arise without any visible, known or explained source or cause.
brief.meaningZh: 看似沒有可見、已知或解釋過的來源原因便出現。
brief.grammar: appear out of thin air; often negative did not appear out of thin air to point to real origins.
brief.register: Common figurative expression, not a supernatural claim.

listening.en: The community garden did not appear out of thin air; residents spent months finding land, sharing tools and planning the work.
listening.zh: 社區花園並非憑空出現；居民花幾個月找地、分享工具及規劃工作。
listening.promptZh: 說話者為甚麼否定憑空出現？

options.en: There was a process of preparation and effort behind it.
options.zh: 背後有準備及努力過程。

options.en: The garden was complete before anyone planned or worked.
options.zh: 任何人規劃或工作前，花園已完成。

options.en: The residents cannot identify any action connected to the garden.
options.zh: 居民無法指出任何與花園相連的行動。

options.en: The lack of an opening ceremony proves there were no origins.
options.zh: 沒有開幕禮證明沒有來源。

reply.promptZh: 花園是突然就有的嗎？
reply.promptEn: Did the garden simply appear without preparation?

options.en: No, residents had worked towards it for months.
options.zh: 不是，居民已為此工作幾個月。

options.en: No, it did not appear out of thin air.
options.zh: 不是，它並非憑空出現。

options.en: No, planning, shared tools and finding land came first.
options.zh: 不是，先有規劃、分享工具及找地。

options.en: No, the finished garden followed a long preparation process.
options.zh: 不是，完成花園之前有長準備過程。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都否定無準備來源；金句不主張超自然。

scene.promptZh: 同學只看到獲獎演出，沒看到之前半年排練。哪句準確提醒有來源？

options.en: The performance did not appear out of thin air; months of rehearsal came before it.
options.zh: 演出並非憑空出現；之前有幾個月排練。

options.en: Not seeing the rehearsals establishes that no preparation happened.
options.zh: 沒看過排練已確定沒有準備。

options.en: The team first began rehearsing after the award ceremony.
options.zh: 團隊在頒獎後才開始排練。

scene.explanationZh: 沒看見過程不等於沒有過程，題目已給半年排練。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個理解最不符合 did not appear out of thin air？

options.en: There were relevant origins or preparation behind the result.
options.zh: 結果背後有相關來源或準備。

options.en: The speaker challenges the impression of a source-free appearance.
options.zh: 說話者挑戰沒有來源便出現的印象。

options.en: The speaker confirms that no cause could be found or have existed.
options.zh: 說話者確認沒有原因可找或可能存在。

contrast.explanationZh: 否定句正相反，提醒有來源而非證實無來源。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「我今天才留意，所以它一定今天才形成」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: Your first notice establishes the date the work began.
options.zh: 你首次留意已確定工作開始日期。

options.en: We should check the earlier records; noticing a result now does not date its creation.
options.zh: 應查早期紀錄；現在留意結果，不決定它形成日期。

options.en: The preparation can be left out because it was not public at the time.
options.zh: 準備當時未公開，所以可略去。

dialogue.explanationZh: 個人察覺時間與事物來源時間不同。

speaking.en: The successful event did not appear out of thin air; volunteers had prepared it for months.
speaking.zh: 成功活動並非憑空出現；義工已準備幾個月。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出可見結果背後的努力。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你第一次看到一款學生設計遊戲，覺得突然很完整；團隊日誌顯示此前有多次測試及修改。用一至兩句英文修正無準備便出現的印象。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用日誌及草稿支持先前發展，區分今天察覺與今天才形成，不只以語氣否定。

examples.en: The finished game did not appear out of thin air; the team’s log records repeated tests and revisions.
examples.zh: 完成的遊戲並非憑空出現；團隊日誌記錄反覆測試與修改。

examples.en: Although I noticed it only today, the game did not appear out of thin air. Earlier drafts show how it developed.
examples.zh: 雖然我今天才留意，遊戲並非憑空出現。早期草稿顯示它怎樣發展。

takeaways.en: The idea did not appear out of thin air; it grew from earlier discussions.
takeaways.zh: 想法並非憑空出現；它從早前討論發展。

takeaways.en: A result may seem to appear out of thin air when the preparation was not visible.
takeaways.zh: 準備過程不顯眼時，結果可能像憑空出現。

titleZh: 賺取或取得足夠資源維持運作

target.pattern: \bkeep(?:s|ing)? the lights on\b|\bkept the lights on\b

brief.meaningEn: Obtain enough income or resources for an organisation to continue operating.
brief.meaningZh: 取得足夠收入或資源，讓機構繼續運作。
brief.grammar: sales/funding/help keep the lights on; past kept; financial-operation idiom.
brief.register: Informal operating-survival expression, not only the electricity bill.
brief.boundaryZh: 不等於高利潤、擴張或財務已穩定；本課虛構機構的整體基本運作，不只實際開燈。
brief.misconceptionZh: 能維持不表示有很多盈餘；活動價值與足夠收入仍是不同考慮。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述基本運作所需支援，區分維持與繁榮。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Ticket sales help the theatre keep the lights on.

listening.en: In the story, the weekly ticket income helped the small cinema keep the lights on by covering its basic running costs, not by funding an expansion.
listening.zh: 故事中，每周票房收入透過支付基本營運費，幫小影院維持運作，而非資助擴張。
listening.promptZh: 這裏收入發揮甚麼作用？

options.en: It covers basic operation rather than proving large profits.
options.zh: 它支付基本運作，而非證明高利潤。

options.en: It has already funded a larger building and extra screens.
options.zh: 它已資助更大建築及更多銀幕。

options.en: It pays old debts while leaving current running costs unfunded.
options.zh: 它支付舊債，當前營運費仍未有資源。

options.en: It shows that running costs no longer need attention.
options.zh: 它顯示不再需留意營運費。

listening.explanationZh: basic running costs 指維持整體運作，明確非擴張。

reply.promptZh: 每周收入對這小影院有甚麼幫助？
reply.promptEn: How does the weekly income help the small cinema?

options.en: It pays the basic costs of continuing the service.
options.zh: 它支付維持服務的基本費用。

options.en: It helps keep the lights on.
options.zh: 它幫助維持運作。

options.en: The cinema can meet its ordinary running expenses.
options.zh: 影院可支付平常營運開支。

options.en: It supports staying open rather than financing a larger site.
options.zh: 它支持繼續開放，而非資助更大場地。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述基本運作，不只電費或高利潤。

scene.promptZh: 虛構社區雜誌的訂閱費剛好支付印製與寄送，還沒有錢擴大刊量。哪句準確？

options.en: Subscriptions help keep the lights on, but do not yet pay for expansion.
options.zh: 訂閱幫助維持運作，卻尚未支付擴張。

options.en: Covering the basic bills confirms that the magazine has a large surplus.
options.zh: 付基本帳單確認雜誌有大量盈餘。

options.en: Subscriptions fund a new edition without covering regular production costs.
options.zh: 訂閱資助新版本，卻未付平常製作費。

scene.explanationZh: 基本營運與盈餘不同，應保留剛好及未擴張。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜單靠 keep the lights on 推斷？

options.en: Basic operations can continue.
options.zh: 基本運作可繼續。

options.en: There is enough support for essential running costs in the stated period.
options.zh: 在所指時段有足夠支援付必要營運費。

options.en: A reserve for next year’s expansion has already been secured.
options.zh: 明年擴張所需的儲備已確保。

contrast.explanationZh: 基本維持不表示已儲備明年擴張資金。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「keep the lights on 就表示資金很多，可以立即擴張」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: A budget that covers basic bills is enough evidence for any expansion.
options.zh: 預算付得起基本帳單，已足以支持任何擴張。

options.en: The phrase says it can keep operating; extra capacity needs separate resources and assessment.
options.zh: 片語說它能繼續運作；額外容量需另外資源及評估。

options.en: We should leave ongoing expenses out of the decision once the first bills are paid.
options.zh: 首次帳單付完，就應把持續開支排除在決定外。

dialogue.explanationZh: 基本維持與額外發展要分清，不能由片語推論盈餘很多。

speaking.en: The subscriptions helped keep the lights on without creating a large surplus.
speaking.zh: 訂閱幫助維持運作，並沒有產生大量盈餘。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清基本維持及額外資源。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區閱讀室靠會員固定支持，支付場租及日常人手，讓附近學生每周仍有安靜地方讀書。你想寫簡短致謝，說明支持如何讓服務繼續，不只列收據。用一至兩句英文表達。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用場租人手與學生可持續使用的服務說明支持作用，採致謝語氣，不把維持營運只解成支付燈泡。

examples.en: Your regular support helps keep the lights on at the reading room, giving local students a quiet place to study each week. Thank you for making that continuing service possible.
examples.zh: 你們固定支持讓閱讀室維持運作，讓附近學生每周有安靜地方讀書。感謝你們讓這服務得以繼續。

examples.en: By helping us cover rent and routine staffing, you keep the lights on for a space the students rely on. We are grateful that we can welcome them back each week.
examples.zh: 你們幫助支付場租及日常人手，讓學生依靠的空間繼續運作。我們感激能每周再歡迎他們。

takeaways.en: Donations helped the fictional centre keep the lights on through the quiet season.
takeaways.zh: 捐助幫虛構中心在淡季維持運作。

takeaways.en: The small paper kept the lights on with subscriptions while postponing its expansion.
takeaways.zh: 小報靠訂閱維持運作，同時押後擴張。
